Rashi on Chullin 90b:10:1.hebrew: השקו את התמיד - כשבאין לשוחטו, משקין אותו, והוא נוח להפשיט:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:10:1.english: They gave the daily offering to drink - When they come to slaughter it, they give it [water] to drink, and it is easy to flay:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:10:2.english: An exaggeration - For [it was] not literally a golden cup:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:11:1.hebrew: לשון הואי - לשון הדיוט שאינו מדקדק בדבריו, ומוציא בפיו דבר שאינו, ולא שיתכון לשקר, אלא לא דק:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:11:1.english: Exaggerated [havai] language - The language of an ordinary person who is not precise in his words, and utters with his mouth something that is not [literally so] — not that he intends to lie, rather he is simply imprecise.

Rashi on Chullin 90b:12:1.hebrew: בשמים - אלמא לא דק. וכן "ותבקע הארץ" דאדוניה, דנראה מקול ההמון כאילו היא נבקעת, אשטורנ"ר בלע"ז:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:12:1.english: Up to heaven - Thus [we see that] it is not exact. And similarly, "[so that] the earth rent" in [the episode of] Adonijah — [meaning] that from the sound of the multitude it seemed as though it [the earth] were splitting open, *estorner* in Old French [to resound/stun]:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:13:1.hebrew: בשלשה מקומות כו' - אבל כוס של זהב דתמיד דווקא הוא, דאין עניות במקום עשירות:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:13:1.english: In three places, etc. - However, the golden cup of the Tamid [offering] is [meant] literally, for there is no poverty in a place of wealth:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:13:2.hebrew: גפן - כמין גפן היה עשוי, שקורין טרייל"א, שמודלה על הכלונסות:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:13:2.english: The vine - It was made like a vine — which they call "treille" [a trellis] — that is trained on poles:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:14:1.english: Three hundred priests - [This is an] exaggeration:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:15:2.hebrew: כ"ד חוטין - מקראי ילפינן במסכת יומא בפרק בא לו כהן גדול (יומא דף עא:), שחוטה כפול עשרים וארבעה:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:15:2.english: Twenty-four threads - We derive from Scriptural verses in Tractate Yoma, in the chapter [entitled] Ba Lo Kohen Gadol (Yoma 71b), that its thread is twenty-four-fold:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:15:3.hebrew: ארכה מ' ורחבה עשרים - ארכה לגובהו של פתח אולם, ורחבה לרחבו, שפתח האולם גובהו מ' ורחבו כ', ופרוכת פרוסה נגדו לצניעות בעלמא; כך שמעתי. ול"נ שאף פרוכת הדביר כך מדתו: רחבו לרחבו של היכל, שהוא כ' אמה, וגבהו לגבהו, מן העלייה ועד הרצפה:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:15:3.english: Its length is forty [cubits] and its width is twenty - its length corresponds to the height of the entrance of the Antechamber [Ulam], and its width to its width, for the entrance of the Antechamber is forty [cubits] high and twenty [cubits] wide, and a curtain is spread across it merely for modesty; so I have heard. But it seems to me that the curtain of the Holy of Holies [Devir] also has this measurement: its width corresponds to the width of the Sanctuary [Heikhal], which is twenty cubits, and its height corresponds to its height, from the upper chamber down to the floor:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:15:4.hebrew: ומשמונים ושתים ריבוא - חוטין. לישנא אחרינא: ריבות, נערות העוסקות בה:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:15:4.english: And from eighty-two ten-thousands - [of] threads. Another interpretation: [it means] riboth, [i.e.,] young women who work on it:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:15:5.hebrew: ושלש מאות כהנים מטבילין אותה - כשהיא נטמאת, והיינו לשון הואי, דלא בעי כולי האי:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:15:5.english: And three hundred priests would immerse it - when it becomes [ritually] impure; and this is exaggerated language, for it does not require that many [priests]:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:16:1.english: And logic dictates - Further on, [the Gemara] asks about it:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:17:1.english: Is it obvious to him - [that it is] of the right [thigh]:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:17:2.english: The logic of the Torah - As it derives further on:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:17:3.hebrew: דעת נוטה - לשון ספק, אבל נראה במקצת, שושפינשי"ר. דסתם הנאבק עם חבירו, כשהוא נותן ימינו לשמאל חבירו וחובקו, ידו מגעת מאחוריו עד ירך ימינו:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:17:3.english: Logic inclines - [This is] an expression of doubt, yet it appears somewhat [probable] — suspenser [in Old French, meaning in suspense/inclined]. For ordinarily, one who wrestles with his fellow, when he places his right [hand] to his fellow's left [side] and embraces him, his hand reaches from behind him to his [fellow's] right thigh:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:18:1.english: The bones and the sinews - of the Paschal offering, or [the] meat that is left over from it:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:18:2.hebrew: ישרפו לששה עשר - ולא בחמשה עשר, דקיימא לן (שבת דף כד:) אין שורפין קדשים ביום טוב. והנך עצמות, כשיש בהן מוח קאמר, ומפני ששמשו את הנותר — דמוח הוי כבשר — ולפיכך טעונין שריפה כנותר עצמו; אבל דלאו בר אכילה אין טעון שריפה, דכתיב "לא תותירו וגו'": כל דקרינן ביה "לא תותירו", קרינן ביה "תשרפו", ואידך לא:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:18:2.english: They should be burned on the sixteenth - and not on the fifteenth [of Nisan], for it is established for us (Shabbat 24b) [that] we do not burn sacred offerings on a Festival. And [regarding] these bones, [the Mishnah] is speaking of when they contain marrow; and because they served [as a vessel for] the leftover [meat] — for marrow is like meat — they therefore require burning like the leftover [meat] itself; but [regarding] that which is not fit for eating, it does not require burning, as it is written: "You shall not leave over, etc." [Exodus 12:10, which concludes: "you shall burn"]: whatever we apply "you shall not leave over" to, we apply "you shall burn" to, and the other [which is not edible] we do not:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:18:3.english: Sinews of meat - all the soft sinews that spread through the meat:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:18:4.english: And let one eat them - on the night of Passover, and why does one leave them over?

Rashi on Chullin 90b:18:5.english: And if [it refers to a case] where they happened to be left over - [the Mishnah] already taught "the leftover" [notar]:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:18:6.hebrew: אלא גידי צואר - דקשין כעצמות, ודרכן לשיירן על כרחו, ואורחא דתנא למתנינהו באנפי נפשייהו כעצמות:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:18:6.english: Rather, sinews of the neck - For they are hard like bones, and [people] inevitably leave them over, and it is the way of the Tanna to teach them separately, like bones:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:18:7.hebrew: לשדינהו - לאשפה, כיון דלאו בשר נינהו:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:18:7.english: Let one discard them - to the garbage heap, since they are not meat:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:19:1.english: And Rav Chisda said - [This is how] we read [the text]:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:19:2.hebrew: ואליבא דר' יהודה - דמספקא ליה הי אסור והי שרי, והלכך על כרחיה משייר להו, ותרוייהו בעי שריפה: לכל חד וחד מספקינן ליה בהיתירא והוי נותר שפיר, משום הכי בעי לשיורינהו ולמשרפינהו:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:19:2.english: And in accordance with [the opinion of] Rabbi Yehudah - For he is uncertain which [one] is forbidden and which is permitted, and therefore he is forced to leave them over, and both require burning: each and every one we treat as possibly the permitted [one], and it is properly [considered] leftover [meat]; therefore, he must leave them over and burn them:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:21:1.english: That they were identified - [This is] not meant literally.

Rashi on Chullin 90b:21:2.english: Became intermingled - [meaning] that they do not know which [nerve] was taken from the right [thigh] and which from the left [thigh]:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:2:1.hebrew: ממשקה ישראל - מקרא הוא בספר יחזקאל: "שה אחד מן הצאן מן המאתים ממשקה ישראל", ולענין קרבנות ונסכיהם כתיב. ומפרשינן ליה בפסחים בפרק אלו עוברין: "מן המותר לישראל", אבל גיד הנשה לא; וכי רבי קרא, פרשו דהיתירא רבי, ולא מחוברין דאיסורא:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:2:1.english: From the well-watered pastures [mimashkeh] of Israel - It is a verse in the Book of Ezekiel: "One lamb from the flock, out of two hundred, from the well-watered pastures of Israel" [Ezekiel 45:15], and it is written regarding offerings and their libations. And we explain it in [Tractate] Pesachim, in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Overin: "[only] from that which is permitted to Israel" — but the sciatic nerve is not [permitted]. And when the verse included [something], it included detached [parts] that are permitted, and not attached [parts] that are forbidden:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:3:1.hebrew: מידי דהוה אחלב ודם - דאסורין לאכול וקרבים לגבוה, וכי כתיב "מן המותר לישראל" — למעוטי טרפה, אבל מין הבשר קרב כולו:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:3:1.english: Just as it is [with forbidden] fat and blood - which are forbidden to eat, yet are offered to the Most High [on the altar]. And when "from that which is permitted to Israel" is written, [it comes] to exclude a tereifah [an animal with a fatal defect], but the species of [permitted] flesh is offered in its entirety:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:3:2.english: Their mitzvah is in this [manner] - Fat and blood are the essence of the sacrifice:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:4:1.hebrew: חולצו (מן התפוח) - חולצו מן הירך ומשליכו לתפוח — צבור האפר שבאמצע המזבח, שהיו גורפין האפר תמיד וצוברין שם, וכשהוא רבה מוציאין אותו לחוץ, והוא נקרא תפוח, כדלקמן בשמעתין:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:4:1.english: He removes it (from the tapuach) - He removes it from the thigh and casts it onto the tapuach — the heap of ashes in the middle of the altar, where they would continually rake the ashes and pile [them] there, and when it grew large they would take it outside, and it is called tapuach, as [stated] later in our sugya:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:4:2.hebrew: מרי דיכי - בעל שמועה זו, הבין דבריך, וכי נאמר "לא יאכל המזבח":
Rashi on Chullin 90b:4:2.english: Master of this [mari dikhi] - [That is:] Master of this teaching, understand your words! Is it indeed stated, "The altar shall not eat [it]"?

Rashi on Chullin 90b:6:1.hebrew: שלמים - שהירך נאכל, חולץ הגיד ומכבדו לאמה שבעזרה, ואינו מצוה לשורפו משום נותר, דכי כתיב שרפה בנותר — בדבר הראויה לאכילה כתיב, כדכתיב (ויקרא יט) "יאכל והנותר ישרף". וקשה לי: ירך של שלמים למה נחתך בעזרה? והלא נאכל בכל העיר? ונראה בעיני ד"חטאת ואשם" גרסינן, שהן נאכלין בעזרה. אי נמי, משום חזה ושוק של כהנים — והגיד בתוכו, ורוב אכילתן ודירתן בעזרה ולשכותיהם ששם היו ישנים — נקט נמי שלמים:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:6:1.english: Peace offerings - Since the thigh is eaten, one removes the sciatic nerve and sweeps it to the drain in the Temple courtyard, and there is no commandment to burn it on account of notar [leftover sacrificial meat], for when burning is written regarding notar, it is written regarding something fit for eating, as it is written (Leviticus 19[:6]): "It shall be eaten... and that which remains shall be burned." And it is difficult for me: Why is the thigh of a peace offering cut up in the Temple courtyard? Is it not eaten throughout the entire city [of Jerusalem]? It appears to me that we should read "a sin offering and a guilt offering" [in the baraita], for they are eaten in the Temple courtyard. Alternatively, because of the breast and thigh [given] to the priests — and the sciatic nerve is within it [the thigh], and most of their eating and dwelling is in the Temple courtyard and their chambers, where they used to sleep — [the baraita] also mentioned peace offerings:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:6:2.hebrew: מעלהו - עם הירך כמות שהיא שלמה, ואח"כ חולצו בראש המזבח, שגנאי הוא להביא ירך מפורעת למזבח, משום "הקריבהו נא לפחתך":
Rashi on Chullin 90b:6:2.english: He brings it up - with the thigh as it is, whole, and afterward removes it on top of the altar, for it is unseemly to bring a cut-open thigh to the altar, because of [the verse], "Present it now to your governor" [Malachi 1:8]:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:9:1.hebrew: כשלש מאות כור - דשן של צבור גדול שמסלקין לו מן הצדדין, קרי "תפוח"; וכן גבי יקב במסכת ע"ז (דף נה:): דורכין עם העובד כוכבים בגת, ואע"ג שנוטל בידו ונותן לתפוח:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:9:1.english: As three hundred kor - A large pile of ashes that they clear [to the center] from the sides [of the altar] is called a tapuach [lit. "apple"/mound]; and similarly regarding a winepress in Tractate Avodah Zarah (55b): one may tread [grapes] with an idolater in a winepress, even though he takes [grapes] in his hand and places [them] onto the tapuach [the pile of grapes in the center]:

Rashi on Chullin 90b:9:2.hebrew: גוזמא - מילתא בעלמא ולאו דווקא, דמעולם לא הגיע לשלש מאות כור:
Rashi on Chullin 90b:9:2.english: An exaggeration [guzma] - A mere figure of speech and not exact, for it never reached three hundred kor:

Tosafot on Chullin 90b:13:1.hebrew: בשלשה מקומות דברו חכמים לשון הואי - אבל ההיא דתמיד (דף ל.), קסבר דאין זה הואי, כדמפרש במסכת תמיד: משום שאין עניות במקום עשירות:
Tosafot on Chullin 90b:13:1.english: In three places the Sages spoke [in] exaggerated language - However, [regarding] that [statement] in Tamid (30a), [Shmuel] holds that this is not an exaggeration, as it explains in tractate Tamid: because there is no poverty in a place of wealth:

Tosafot on Chullin 90b:15:1.hebrew: שלש מאות כהנים מטבילין אותה - וא"ת: דאמר סוף פ"ק דביצה (דף יד:): מפני מה אמרו וילון טמא? מפני שהשמש מתחמם כנגדו; והאי פרוכת ליכא למיחש שיתחממו כנגדו, דאסור ליהנות ממנו, ואמאי מטבילין אותה? וליכא למימר דכיון שנארגה היו מטבילין אותה, כדאמר בפ' חומר בקדש (חגיגה דף כג.) דכלים הנגמרים בטהרה צריכין טבילה לקדש; דהתם לא מיירי אלא בכלים המקבלין טומאה, דמשום חומר הקדש החמירו להטבילן כאילו נטמאו, אבל פרוכת דלא מקבל טומאה — לא! ועוד, דבמסכת שקלים בפרק כל הרוקין (דף יב:) משמע בהדיא דפרוכת מקבל טומאה, דתנן: פרוכת שנטמא באב הטומאה מטבילין אותה בחוץ, נטמא בולד הטומאה מטבילין אותה בפנים. וי"ל דמקבל טומאה לפי שהוא אהל, כדאמר בפרק קמא דסוכה (דף ז:): "וסכות על הארון" — דכייף ליה מיכף עילויה דארון. ומיהו יש ספרים דגרסי בפרק קמא דביצה (דף יד:): מפני מה וילון אסור? וכן גרסינן בהלכות גדולות; פירוש: מפני מה אסור לעשות וילון מכלאים:
Tosafot on Chullin 90b:15:1.english: Three hundred priests would immerse it - And if you ask: [The Gemara] says at the end of the first chapter of Beitzah (14b): Why did they say a curtain is [susceptible to] impurity? Because the attendant warms himself against it. Now [regarding] this Curtain, there is no concern that they will warm themselves against it, because it is forbidden to derive benefit from it; so why do they immerse it? And one cannot say that as soon as it was woven they would immerse it, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Chomer BaKodesh (Chagigah 23a), that vessels finished in purity require immersion for sacred [use]; for there it speaks only of vessels that are susceptible to impurity, where because of the stringency of sacred [things] they were stringent to immerse them as if they had become impure, whereas a Curtain, which is not susceptible to impurity — no. And furthermore, in tractate Shekalim, in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaRokin (12b), it is explicitly implied that a Curtain is susceptible to impurity, as we learned [in a mishna]: A Curtain that became impure through a primary source of impurity, they immerse it outside; [if] it became impure through a derivative impurity, they immerse it inside. And one can answer that it is susceptible to impurity because it is [considered] a tent, as [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Sukkah (7b): "And you shall screen the Ark" — for it bends over above the Ark. However, there are texts that read in the first chapter of Beitzah (14b): Why is a curtain forbidden? And so we read in Halakhot Gedolot; meaning: why is it forbidden to make a curtain out of kilayim [mingled wool and linen]:

Tosafot on Chullin 90b:8:1.hebrew: של שלמים מכבדו לאמה - פירש בקונטרס דגרסינן "חטאת ואשם", משום דשלמים נאכלים בכל העיר, ומה טיבו בעזרה? ונראה, משום דשוק וחזה ניתן לכהנים, ששם גיד הנשה — שהשוק הוא ברגל ולא ביד, כדתנן לקמן בהזרוע (חולין דף קלד:) — והם היו רגילין לאכול מתנותיהם בעזרה. א"נ, בשלמים של כהנים, שכל קדשיהם היו רגילין לאכול בעזרה:
Tosafot on Chullin 90b:8:1.english: Of a peace offering, one sweeps it into the drain - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained that we read [in the text] "a sin offering and a guilt offering," because peace offerings are eaten throughout the entire city [of Jerusalem], so what would it be doing in the Temple courtyard? However, it appears [that the reading "peace offering" is correct] because the thigh and breast are given to the priests — where the sciatic nerve is [located], for the thigh is on the hind leg and not on the foreleg, as we learned in the Mishnah later in [the chapter] HaZeroa (Chullin 134b) — and they were accustomed to eat their [priestly] gifts in the Temple courtyard. Alternatively, [it is speaking] of peace offerings belonging to priests, for all their sacred [offerings] they were accustomed to eat in the Temple courtyard:
